en.title: The new Halloween video game has been banned in Australia – and not because of the violence
en.description: Academics and a former classification board director say Halloween: The Game’s ban due to ‘incentivised drug use’ highlights an incoherent set of s...
en.fullContent:
Academics and a former classification board director say Halloween: The Game’s ban due to ‘incentivised drug use’ highlights an incoherent set of standards

Halloween’s Michael Myers is one of film’s most feared boogeymen, responsible for some of the most brutal on-screen deaths in horror cinema. The US video game developer Illfonic looked to reproduce those terrors in its upcoming title Halloween: The Game, with gruesome killings a major focus of the gameplay: for instance, you can stomp another player’s head through a toilet seat, or fry their brain by throwing them through a television screen.

But Australians will not be able to play Halloween, because it has been refused classification by the Australian Classification Board, which means it is banned from sale within the country. And it’s not because of the violence or murders.

In the game, players can smoke marijuana to see the location of Michael Myers in order to avoid being killed – a use of drugs that the Classification Board has deemed a “gameplay advantage”. Under the Guidelines for the Classification of Computer Games 2023, video games are refused classification if they contain “illicit or proscribed drug use related to incentives or rewards”.

“Halloween: The Game contains illicit drug use that is linked to an incentive or reward, in that use of the drug provides a gameplay advantage to the player. It is on this basis that the game has been refused classification, as required under the Code and Guidelines,” the board wrote in a recent statement.

In the wake of the decision, Illfonic’s social media accounts have been flooded with comments from irate Australians. An FoI officer said the Classification Board had received more than 500 complaints in relation to Halloween: The Game.

en.title: Gamescom Opening Night Live: All the big news and reveals
en.description: Final Fantasy 7, The Witcher 3 Remastered, and more featured in Geoff Keighley’s show
en.fullContent:
Final Fantasy 7, The Witcher 3 Remastered, and more featured in Geoff Keighley’s show

Gamescom’s annual premiere, Opening Night Live, took place on Tuesday, with updates on upcoming games and a handful of new announcements.

Notably, CD Projekt announced a remaster of The Witcher 3, Square Enix premiered a new look at Final Fantasy 7 Revelations, Xbox showed new footage of Gears of War E-Day, and more.

There were also reveals from Ubisoft, Capcom, Konami, Hoyoverse, Wizards of the Coasts, and more.

Read on for our roundup of all the biggest reveals and announcements at Gamescom Opening Night Live.

Hoyoverse announced Nodus Fall, an original co-op action game.

en.title: GTA 6 leaks: Rockstar issues statement over online clips
en.description: Grand Theft Auto 6 maker Rockstar Games has issued a statement addressing a series of leaked videos showing the upcoming blockbuster video game.
en.fullContent:
Grand Theft Auto 6 maker Rockstar Games has issued a statement addressing a series of leaked videos showing the upcoming blockbuster video game.

Clips appearing to show gameplay and cinematics from the title began appearing online last week, but the developer did not acknowledge them straight away.

In a statement, the company said the leaks had been "heartbreaking" for the team working on the sequel, and that they were "not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time".

The company apologised for the delays in releasing official updates on the highly anticipated title, but vowed to "exceed" fans' expectations in a special preview airing on Netflix this week.

When leaks first began to surface, there was some doubt as to whether they were genuine.

But as the days went on, evidence mounted to suggest they were legitimate.

en.title: 'GTA VI' Cyberleek update: Everything leaked Tuesday, this week
en.description: Alleged clips of Grand Theft Auto VI simply cannot stop leaking onto the internet.
en.fullContent:
Alleged clips of Grand Theft Auto VI simply cannot stop leaking onto the internet.

After a few clips came out over the weekend and into Monday, there are now a few more, courtesy of the now-notorious leaker known as Cyberleek. As Rockstar and Take-Two step up their efforts to find and stop Cyberleek, clips keep coming out at an even more rapid pace.

We're not going to embed or link directly to any of these clips, but they are easy to find on social media. As of Tuesday morning, three new clips have surfaced:

A clip of protagonist Jason riding a bicycle on a beach packed with civilian NPCs

A clip of Jason looking around a fictional video game retailer, complete with a bunch of fake video game boxes

That brings the total number of leaked clips to 13, at the time of publication. To be clear, their authenticity has not been totally verified, but Rockstar and parent company Take-Two's legal efforts to stop them from coming out is certainly telling in that regard. In subpoenas, Take-Two has referred to the Cyberleek videos as "stolen content" and "leaked gameplay videos," suggesting they could be authentic.

en.title: GTA 6 leaks ‘far less consequential’ than Hot Coffee sex scandal, claims former Rockstar developer
en.description: A former GTA developer claims this month’s leaks are a “tiny blip” to Rockstar
en.fullContent:
A former GTA developer claims this month’s leaks are a “tiny blip” to Rockstar

A former Grand Theft Auto developer has played down the impact of this month’s big GTA6 leaks, claiming that the online footage is “far less consequential” to the company than the infamous ‘Hot Coffee’ scandal of the early 2000s.

Last week, a mysterious group known as ‘Cyberleek’ began posting what appears to be authentic gameplay clips from Grand Theft Auto 6, days before an official Netflix reveal planned for later this month.

Rockstar parent Take-Two Interactive has scrambled to put a stop to the short clips with DMCA strikes and subpoenas petitioning Microsoft and Discord for information that could lead to the leaker, but so far this does not appear to have stopped the leaks.

Obbe Vermeij, who was technical director at Rockstar for the development of GTA 3, Vice City, San Andreas, and GTA 4, suggested on social media that this month’s leaks will be affecting management more than GTA 6’s development team, arguing that most of GTA 6’s potential audience won’t even know they exist.

“Calm down everybody. The leaks are a nothing burger,” he wrote. “As a marketing strategy R* is trying to keep the game under wraps longer than other publishers. All that has happened is that some footage has escaped. Slightly ahead of the Netflix thing next week.
